connector: Last time, Lucy woke the others, and they couldn’t see what she saw. Today they follow her through the dark, one by one, and some of them begin to see. Line up the choices from both chapters. What one word fits all of them?

a.raw: oh aslan said king peter im so glad
a.why: Peter’s real words in Chapter 11. Capitals on Oh, Aslan, King Peter and I’m; quotation marks around each part he says; commas separate his words from said King Peter; the period goes inside the quotation mark.

b.raw: lucy said susan in a very small voice
b.fixed: “Lucy,” said Susan in a very small voice.
b.why: Lewis’s own sentence. Capitals on Lucy and Susan; the comma goes inside the quotation mark after Lucy; a period ends it.

scholar.journal-q1: … and quote what else Susan says to Lucy.
scholar.journal-q2: … and describe one tree-person Lewis shows you.

notes.wgrd: Put the echoes side by side: list each choice from Ch. 10 and 11, find one word that fits them all, and test it on every line.
vocab: A very steep cliff or drop.
A rough camp without proper shelter.
Able to feel and sense things; aware.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: rupt = break, duct and duce = lead, form = shape: interrupt, conduct, introduce, transform.
notes.grammar: Commas in dates and places: a comma between the day and the year (June 12, 1941), between a town and its county or country (Dover, Kent), and another after them if the sentence goes on. Narnia has no calendar, so practice dates are made up.
notes.spelling: Greek and Latin parts you know: port (carry), spect (look), script and scribe (write), rupt (break), tele (far). Spell the part the same way every time: inter + rupt + ion.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: In Chapter 11 the others begin to see Aslan. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Susan says to Lucy in a very small voice, “I see him now. I’m sorry.” Then: “But I’ve been far worse than you know.”
items.why: She admits more than anyone asked her to.

items.t: Peter drops on one knee before Aslan: “I’m so glad. And I’m so sorry. I’ve been leading them wrong ever since we started.”
items.why: The High King owns his mistake out loud.
items.hint: What is hard about a king saying this?

items.t: Aslan welcomes Edmund with two words: “Well done.” Edmund was the one who voted to believe Lucy at the gorge.
items.why: He stood by his sister when the vote went against her.
items.hint: What did Edmund do in Chapter 9?

items.t: Lucy follows Aslan through the dark, keeping her eyes on him, while the others stumble after her and can’t see him yet.
items.why: She keeps following when she is the only one who can see.

transcripts.welcome: Hello again, it’s Nell. The others are following Lucy through the dark, and they still can’t see what she sees. Today’s question: what do all of this week’s choices have in common?
transcripts.read: Line up the choices: Lucy following, Susan admitting, Peter kneeling. Find one word that fits all of them. Then, when Aslan roars, slow down. Watch what the trees do, and who they turn into.
transcripts.grammar: Commas in dates and places. A date: June 12, 1941. The comma sits between the day and the year. A place: Dover, Kent. The comma sits between the town and the bigger place it belongs to. If the sentence keeps going, add one more comma after.
